# All three edge ears strictly improve a tight triangular Lorentz row

This note completes the local ear calculation at a triangle saturating one ordinary planar Lorentz row. It proves no inequality for a general finite ear or arbitrary body, and does not preserve mixed-fiber compatibility or fixed sector areas.

## 1. The actual triangle and the two new ear families

Use v1=(1,0), v2=(0,1), v3=(-1,-1), source zero, and

    P1=(2v+w,-v-w), P2=(-x,x+s), P3=(-x,-s-w),
    x,s,v>0, w>=0.

These parametrize every strict-incidence triangle saturating Lorentz row 1, after exchanging rows 2 and 3 if necessary, as proved in `candidate cfb017a0e12acfbf`. Put

    p=2v+w, L=x+p, H=x+s+w+v, B=x+2s+w,
    b=x+s, c=x+s+w, k=LB/2.

For any body define Qi, sigma_i, M, Fi and Phi_i as in that source:

    M=sum Qi/sigma_i, Fi=2 sqrt(k Qi)/(sigma_i M),
    Phi_i=Fi+(Fj+Fk)^2/4.

At this triangle M=H, F1=L/H and F2=F3=sqrt(B/H), so Phi1=2.

There are two families to check. In family j=2, the old edge is P1P3 and the new tip is in the double-signature sector of caps 1 and 3. In family j=3, use edge P1P2 and the double-signature sector of caps 1 and 2. Define the negative and positive heights for the second affected cap by

    (n_j,c_j)=(v,c)       if j=2,
    (n_j,c_j)=(v+w,b)     if j=3.

In each case c_j+n_j=H. Parameterize the base of the new tip as

    Q0=(1-theta)P1+theta P_l,  {1,j,l}={1,2,3},
    n_j/H<=theta<=p/L.                                  (1)

Its two captured heights are p-L theta and H theta-n_j, both nonnegative. The interval has positive length: pH-n_2 L>0 and pH-n_3 L=sp+vx>0. Its endpoints are strictly between zero and one, so Q0 is always in the relative interior of the old edge, including at the two cut-crossing endpoints of (1).

For epsilon>=0 set

    Q_epsilon=Q0+(epsilon/k)(Q0-P_j),
    K_epsilon=conv(P1,P2,P3,Q_epsilon).                 (2)

For epsilon>0 this is an actual convex quadrilateral. Its diagonals P1P_l and P_jQ_epsilon cross at Q0 in their relative interiors. Its added triangle has area exactly epsilon, since its altitude is epsilon/k times the old opposite altitude. The original triangle remains contained, so the source stays interior. The tip belongs to the strict intended double-signature sector even at the endpoint choices in (1): both affected normals are negative at P_j, and the displacement moves their nonnegative values strictly upward. The unaffected cap remains unchanged. Thus no boundary-tip seam is suppressed.

## 2. First variation from actual cap and coarea formulas

Let a prime mean the derivative at epsilon=0. Write n=n_j and z=c_j temporarily. The first affected cap has positive old vertex height p and negative height x. The other has positive height z and negative height n. The ordinary added-ear clipping formula gives

    Q1'=1-x^2/[L^2(1-theta)],
    sigma1'=2x/[L^2(1-theta)],
    Ql'=1-n^2/[H^2 theta],
    sigma_l'=2n/[H^2 theta],
    Qj'=sigma_j'=0, k'=1.                               (3)

Indeed the new apex heights at epsilon zero are p-L theta and H theta-n. Their changes with epsilon multiply the already vanishing ear area and so do not affect these first derivatives. The exact ear formulas have positive denominators at both endpoints of (1), proving the claimed derivatives there as well.

The old data are Q1=p^2B/(2L), sigma1=pB/L, Ql=Lz^2/(2H), sigma_l=Lz/H. Therefore

    M'=(p-L theta)/[(1-theta)pB]
           +(H theta-n)/[theta Lz].                     (4)

Differentiating the definition of the Fi, using F2=F3, now yields

    D_j:=Phi1'
      =(4-L/H)[1/(LB)-M'/H]
       +(L/H)[Q1'/(2Q1)-sigma1'/sigma1]
       +(B/H)[Ql'/(2Ql)-sigma_l'/sigma_l].               (5)

The next section proves D_j<0 for both j and the whole closed interval (1).

## 3. Exact sign certificates

Write

    Z_j=pH-n_j L,
    theta=n_j/H+u[p/L-n_j/H],  0<=u<=1,
    A_j(u)=n_j L+u Z_j,
    B_j(u)=L c_j-u Z_j.

Thus A_j=HL theta and B_j=HL(1-theta) are strictly positive. Define

    Den_j=p^2 c_j^2 B L H^2 A_j(u) B_j(u)>0.

Define a strictly positive quartic by its square-completed expression

    Pstar=(2sp-x^2/4)^2+15x^4/16
       +s(4w+2x)p^2+s x^3+p^2w(w+x)+vp x^2+(v+w)x^3.

The following positive cubics will also be used:

    Pplus=2s^2v+s^2w+s^2x+2svw+2svx+2sw^2+4swx+2sx^2
        +vw^2+2vwx+vx^2+w^3+3w^2x+3wx^2+x^3;
    Pminus=2s^2v+s^2w+s^2x+2svw+2svx+2sw^2+2sx^2
        +vw^2+vx^2+w^3+x^3.

Finally define R_j=2s^3p^2L+s^2 E_j+s F_j+G_j, where every displayed coefficient below is positive:

    E2=40v^3w+32v^3x+60v^2w^2+64v^2wx+12v^2x^2
       +30vw^3+44vw^2x+16vwx^2+2vx^3+5w^4+10w^3x+5w^2x^2;
    F2=32v^3w^2+44v^3wx+16v^3x^2+48v^2w^3+84v^2w^2x
       +44v^2wx^2+8v^2x^3+24vw^4+55vw^3x+42vw^2x^2
       +15vwx^3+4vx^4+4w^5+12w^4x+12w^3x^2+4w^2x^3;
    G2=(w+x)[8v^3w^2+8v^3wx+4v^3x^2+12v^2w^3+18v^2w^2x
       +10v^2wx^2+4v^2x^3+6vw^4+13vw^3x+10vw^2x^2
       +5vwx^3+2vx^4+w^5+3w^4x+3w^3x^2+w^2x^3];

    E3=8v^3w+32v^3x+12v^2w^2+56v^2wx+12v^2x^2
       +6vw^3+36vw^2x+8vwx^2+2vx^3+w^4+8w^3x+w^2x^2+2wx^3;
    F3=x[20v^3w+16v^3x+40v^2w^2+28v^2wx+8v^2x^2
       +29vw^3+18vw^2x+5vwx^2+4vx^3+7w^4+4w^3x+w^2x^2+4wx^3];
    G3=x[4v^3w^2+4v^3wx+4v^3x^2+10v^2w^3+8v^2w^2x
       +6v^2wx^2+4v^2x^3+8vw^4+7vw^3x+2vw^2x^2
       +5vwx^3+2vx^4+2w^5+2w^4x+2w^2x^3+2wx^4].

Set

    Cj0=n_j^2 c_j^2 L^2 Pstar,
    Cj1=p c_j L H R_j/2,
    C22=x^2 p^2 H^3 Pplus,
    C32=x^2 p^2 H^3 Pminus.

Here the last two equations specify Cj2 for j=2,3. Clearing the denominators in (3)–(5) gives the exact two identities

    -Den_j D_j=Cj0(1-u)^2+2Cj1 u(1-u)+Cj2 u^2,
    j=2,3.                                               (6)

Every coefficient Cjr is strictly positive for x,s,v>0,w>=0. Therefore D_j<0 on the entire closed tip interval. The identities are obtained by rational expansion; their displayed positive factors supply a symbolic certificate valid for every parameter, not a finite sample argument.

## 4. Consequence and precise scope

The two edge families (2) strictly improve the selected tight row for sufficiently small positive epsilon. If the other two rows are strict initially, continuity preserves them. If either is an equality initially, then F1=F2=F3=1, as in the opposite-edge lemma; all three row derivatives equal F1'+F2'+F3'=D_j<0. Hence all three rows become strict.

Together with the already proved opposite-edge calculation, this proves strict first-order improvement for ears on every edge of a tight strict-incidence triangle when the new tip is in that edge's double-signature sector. It rules out this particular local route to a counterexample. It does not prove finite-ear monotonicity, arbitrary-quadrilateral inequalities, or the mixed-integer conjecture.
